title: The RBI Hopes For The Best
text:
The RBI Hopes For The Best

Udith Sikand, Tom Miller

Gavekal Research | 5 Aug 2026

The Reserve Bank of India left its benchmark repo rate unchanged at 5.25% and retained its neutral policy stance, declining to follow the hawkish approach taken by many other central banks.Despite multiple headwinds, India’s economy maintained decent momentum in the April-June quarter. Industrial output rose at the fastest pace in more than two years, with strong growth in the electricity and manufacturing sectors. Bank credit accelerated on strong demand from corporates. Meanwhile, inflation—although steadily creeping higher—remained within the RBI’s target band of 2-6%, allowing India to avoid the pro-cyclical tightening forced upon the likes of Indonesia and the Philippines.
